# LEGION-247 plan: split `@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy` into `@sjawhar/pi-envoy` and `@sjawhar/pi-legion`

The spec is `dispatch://LEGION-247/artifact/spec` (approved v4). This plan follows its design; it departs from nothing (the `specDepartures` record is empty). One issue, one pull request, commits in the order of the work sections below: the shared interface first, while both entries still live in `packages/pi-envoy`; then the package split; then the Go gate; then the release, image and e2e consumers; then the docs and the name check. Commit 1 and the finished head are green on their own; commits 2 to 4 each repair what the previous one moved (the Go real-binary fixtures, the Dockerfile and the e2e pack script still name the old layout until commits 3 and 4), which is fine for a squash-merged pull request and is why the order is fixed.

## What a reader loses and keeps

A person who today installs one package for Dispatch tools and Envoy messaging installs `@sjawhar/pi-envoy` instead; their sessions no longer load Legion's code. A Legion deployment installs both packages into the daemon's Oh My Pi profile; a worker image carries both. Someone who keeps `@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy` keeps the last 7.x release, which works but gets no fixes; a Legion pane that still has it installed beside the new packages is refused by the daemon's gate, by name, with the uninstall as the remedy.

## Repository skills this plan follows

`skill://legion-worker` (phase mechanics, the one push procedure, the PR body and proof rules; `references/systematic-rename.md` for the name sweep), `skill://dispatch` (the plan document and the asks the architect opens), `skill://ce-simplify-code` (the implementer's simplify pass after the change settles). The root `AGENTS.md` verification norms: drive the changed behaviour through its real surface; jj, never git; `bunx biome check`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun test` per package; `go test ./...` in `packages/daemon`.

## Design decisions the spec leaves to the plan

### D1. A third workspace package holds the interface and the modules both entries use

`packages/pi-shared`, npm name `@legion/pi-shared`, `private: true`, no `files`, `bun`/`types` exports to `src/*.ts` like `@legion/envoy-client`'s. Both plugins take it as a `workspace:*` devDependency and `bun build` inlines it into each bundle (the only externals stay `@oh-my-pi/*`), exactly as `@legion/contracts` and `@legion/envoy-client` are inlined today. Its inventory, every file moved from `packages/pi-envoy` unless marked new:

| `packages/pi-shared/src/` | from | why it is shared |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interface.ts` (new) | — | the versioned interface: key, version, types, publish/read (D2) |
| `pi-types.ts` | `src/pi-types.ts` | host types both entries import |
| `omp-host.d.ts` | `extensions/omp-host.d.ts` | ambient `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` declarations; each plugin's tsconfig `include`s it |
| `role-claim-bridge.ts` | `src/legion/role-claim-bridge.ts` | the bridge's types, `claimEnvoyRole`, `subscribeLegionNotice`, `onEnvoyRoleRegained`, the test reset; the bridge object itself now lives on the interface (D2) |
| `injected-user-turns.ts` (split) | `src/dispatch-user-turn.ts` lines defining `INJECTED_USER_TURNS`, `noteInjectedUserTurn`, `matchInjectedUserTurn`, `endInjectedUserTurns`, `resetInjectedUserTurnsForTests` | written by envoy.ts, read by both; the candidate/accept half (`isUserTurnCandidate`, `turnFromAccept`, `handledAttempt*`) stays in pi-envoy |
| `subagent-session.ts` | `src/subagent-session.ts` | `subagentSessionCheck` gates hooks in both entries; its record moves onto the interface |
| `tool-result.ts` | `src/tool-result.ts` | `toolSuccess`/`toolFailure` are used by `src/legion/tools.ts` and `extensions/envoy.ts` |
| `test/omp-harness.ts`, `test/omp-natives.ts`, `test/omp-natives.test.ts`, `test/host-registry.ts` | `extensions/test-*.ts` | the real-binary harness and the roster stand-in both packages' tests use; `spawnRpc` takes absolute extension paths (callers pass `path.join(import.meta.dir, …)`), since `import.meta.dir` no longer points at the caller |

`envoy-session.ts`, `dispatch-first.ts`, `agent-stream.ts`, `opens-ask.ts`, `side-turn.ts` stay in pi-envoy (only envoy.ts imports them). `src/legion/phase-stall.ts` stays Legion; `LOCAL_ENVOY_NOTICE` moves to `interface.ts` and both import it from there.

The rule "neither package imports the other's source" governs shipped code: every non-test file under `extensions/` and `src/` of each plugin. The check is a test in each plugin (`src/no-cross-import.test.ts`, one shared helper in pi-shared `test/cross-imports.ts`) that reads every `.ts` under `extensions/` and `src/` except `*.test.ts` and fails on an import whose resolved path leaves the package directory for the sibling plugin's directory. The two cross-entry tests (`legion-role-claim.test.ts`, `legion-phase-stall-omp.test.ts`) live in pi-legion and reach `../../pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts` by relative path: test-only, allowed by that rule, and what the spec's CI proof needs.

### D2. The interface: one process-wide object, created by whoever touches it first, owned by the Envoy entry that publishes into it

`interface.ts`:

```ts
export const ENVOY_PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION = 1;
export const ENVOY_PLUGIN_INTERFACE_KEY = Symbol.for("legion.pi-shared.envoy-plugin-interface");
export const LEGION_PLUGIN_LOADED_KEY = Symbol.for("legion.pi-legion.loaded");
/** The pre-split package's Legion marker; its presence means @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy is loaded. */
export const LEGACY_LEGION_LOADED_KEY = Symbol.for("legion.pi-envoy.legion-loaded");
export const LOCAL_ENVOY_NOTICE = { localNotice: true } as const;
export interface EnvoyPluginInterface {
  readonly version: number;
  /** import.meta.url of each Envoy entry that published, in publish order; empty until one does. */
  readonly publishers: string[];
  readonly roleClaim: LegionRoleClaimBridge;        // { instances: [], managedSessions: Set, regained }
  readonly injectedUserTurns: Map<string, SessionUserTurns>;
  readonly bootstrappedSession: { file: string | undefined };
}
export function envoyPluginInterface(): EnvoyPluginInterface;             // get-or-create at this build's version
export function publishEnvoyPluginInterface(from: string): EnvoyPluginInterface | undefined;
export function readEnvoyPluginInterface(): { kind: "present"; iface } | { kind: "absent" } | { kind: "mismatch"; found: number; expected: number; from: string };
export function resetEnvoyPluginInterfaceForTests(): void;
```

- Every consumer resolves the object lazily at each use through `envoyPluginInterface()` — `claimEnvoyRole`, `subscribeLegionNotice`, `onEnvoyRoleRegained`, `noteInjectedUserTurn`/`matchInjectedUserTurn`/`endInjectedUserTurns`, `recordBootstrappedSession` and the transcript check in `subagentSessionCheck`. Publish and read order are therefore irrelevant: Oh My Pi gives no cross-plugin factory order this repository can cite, and `legion-role-claim.test.ts` initialises Legion before Envoy on purpose; that test moves unchanged in substance.
- `envoyPluginInterface()` creates the object only when the key is empty, at this build's version with `publishers: []`; when the key holds another version it returns that object anyway (consumers never throw on a version), so a non-Legion session with a mismatched pair never fails.
- The interface carries only process-wide state (the arrays, the map, the record holder), never a per-instance function: Oh My Pi re-binds every extension factory for each in-process `task` subagent, which is the bug `docs/solutions/envoy/heartbeat-role-reassertion-and-regain-hooks.md` records. `envoyExtension(pi)` calls `publishEnvoyPluginInterface(import.meta.url)` at factory time and, as today, pushes its `LegionRoleClaimInstance` onto `iface.roleClaim.instances` of the returned object and splices it out on `session_shutdown`.
- `publishEnvoyPluginInterface(from)`: key empty → create and record `from`; same version → record `from` (a second Envoy instance, a subagent's or a second copy, joins); another version → `logger.warn` once naming both versions and both URLs, return `undefined`, and that instance pushes nothing (first wins). This is what keeps this repository's own dev checkout usable, where the root manifest's `./packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts` loads beside the installed `dist/envoy.js`.
- `readEnvoyPluginInterface()`: `absent` when the key is empty or `publishers` is empty (the object exists only because a Legion consumer created it), `mismatch` when `version !== ENVOY_PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION` (with the first publisher's URL), else `present`.
- Bump rule, written in `packages/pi-shared/AGENTS.md`: any change to the shape of `EnvoyPluginInterface` or to what either side reads from it bumps `ENVOY_PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION`; both plugins release from the same commit, and the daemon's gate refuses a pair that does not match (D4).

`extensions/legion.ts`:
- Factory: `globalThis[LEGION_PLUGIN_LOADED_KEY] = { from: import.meta.url, envoyInterface: ENVOY_PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION }` (replaces the old marker; the Go probe reads this object).
- `session_start`, after the subagent check and `classifySession`, for every Legion kind (root, worker, controller): `verifyEnvoyPlugin()`: if `LEGACY_LEGION_LOADED_KEY` is set → one `logger.error` naming this entry's URL, the old entry's URL and the remedy "uninstall @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy", then `exitProcess(1)`; if `readEnvoyPluginInterface()` is not `present` → one `logger.error` naming `@sjawhar/pi-envoy`, the expected version and the found version or "none", then `exitProcess(1)`, the path `exitOnRegistrationRefusal` already uses for a refused boot. A `not-legion` session returns before this, as today, so a person's own session never exits.
- `/legion-claim-controller` (registered at factory time, usable from a hand-started session): runs the same check first and, on failure, answers the command with that sentence (`ctx.ui.notify` / the command's error return) instead of claiming; never exits.
- `recordBootstrappedSession` is called only after the check passed (claim-session bootstrap, controller session), so it writes into an interface that exists.

### D3. The Legion package and the skills partition

`packages/pi-legion` (`@sjawhar/pi-legion`): `extensions/legion.ts`; `src/` ← `packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/*` (flattened: `claim-session.ts`, `classify.ts`, `controller-session.ts`, `daemon-client.ts`, `grant-file.ts`, `handoff-actions.ts`, `jj-attribution.ts`, `phase-stall.ts`, `session-title.ts`, `tools.ts` and their tests); `agents/` ← `packages/pi-envoy/agents/`; `scripts/grant-rig/`, `scripts/skill-scenarios/` (Legion rigs); tests `extensions/legion.test.ts`, `legion-role-claim.test.ts`, `legion-phase-stall-omp.test.ts`, `src/shipped-agents.test.ts`, `src/daemon-api-version.test.ts`, `src/skills-guard.test.ts` (its Legion half, D3 below). Manifest: `version` as pi-envoy's today, `omp.extensions: ["extensions/legion.ts"]`, `omp.skills: ["dist/skills"]`, `legion.daemonApiVersion: 12`, `files: ["dist","agents"]`, `build`/`prepack`/`postpack`/`typecheck`/`test`/`lint` scripts, devDependencies as pi-envoy's plus `@legion/pi-shared`. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (D7).

`packages/pi-envoy` keeps `extensions/envoy.ts`, `envoy-message-renderer.ts`, `envoy-whoami-command.ts`, `envoy.test.ts`, `dispatch-first-omp.test.ts`, `src/{agent-stream,dispatch-first,dispatch-user-turn,envoy-session,opens-ask,side-turn}.ts` and tests, `scripts/{smoke-btw,smoke-delivery}.sh`, `scripts/README.md`. Manifest renamed `@sjawhar/pi-envoy`, `omp.extensions: ["extensions/envoy.ts"]`, no `legion` key, `files: ["dist"]`.

Skills: one script replaces `packages/pi-envoy/scripts/prepack.sh`: `scripts/pi-plugin-prepack.sh` at the repository root, run from a plugin directory as its `prepack`. It reads the manifest's `omp.extensions` (refuses unless it is exactly `["dist/<entry>.js"]` for the package's one entry), builds that entry with the same `bun build` flags and metafile, writes `dist/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`, and stages into `dist/skills` only that package's skill directories. The partition lives in the script, keyed by package name (a manifest field would be one more thing the gate has to know): `@sjawhar/pi-envoy` → `dispatch dispatch-first dispatch-brainstorming envoy`; `@sjawhar/pi-legion` → `legion-architect legion-controller legion-oracle legion-retro legion-worker ce-simplify-code thermonuclear-code-quality thermonuclear-deep-review`. `scripts/pi-plugin-prepack.sh --stage-skills <package name> <dest>` stages that partition alone, for tests. The two lists must partition `skills/` exactly (every directory in one list, none in both): `packages/pi-shared/test/skills-partition.test.ts` asserts it.

The four relative cross-partition links (`skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:80,87,115`, `skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md:168`, `../dispatch/SKILL.md#…`) become `skill://dispatch/SKILL.md#…`, which resolve by name through discovery when both plugins are installed, as every other cross-skill link does. The skills guard splits: shared logic (`files`, `outsideFences`, the `skill://` link check, the size rules) moves to `packages/pi-shared/test/skills-guard.ts`; `packages/pi-envoy/src/skills-guard.test.ts` runs it over pi-envoy's staged partition plus the `dispatch-first` budget check; `packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts` runs it over pi-legion's staged partition, the daemon's prompts as linking roots, and the legion-worker reference rules. Both add one rule: a relative Markdown link (`](../…)`) inside a staged partition must resolve inside that partition, which is the check that catches the next dangling link.

`envoy.ts` keeps resolving `dist/skills` beside the bundle or `../../../skills` in the repository and reading `dist/skills/dispatch-first/SKILL.md` at load; both layouts still hold the file.

### D4. The Go gate: one Legion manifest, the Envoy plugin proven by the load probe, three new refusals in every lane

`packages/daemon/internal/daemon/probe.mjs` prints, from `globalThis` alone (it imports nothing of pi-shared; the symbol strings are the wire, documented in `packages/pi-shared/AGENTS.md` and beside the constants in `bootgate.go`):

```
LEGION_PLUGIN_LOADED=yes|no
LEGION_PLUGIN_LOADED_FROM=<legion.ts URL>             (when yes)
LEGION_PLUGIN_ENVOY_INTERFACE=<N the Legion entry expects>   (when yes)
LEGION_ENVOY_INTERFACE=<M>|none                      (none: key empty or no publisher)
LEGION_ENVOY_LOADED_FROM=<first publisher's URL>      (when not none)
LEGION_LEGACY_PLUGIN_LOADED_FROM=<URL>               (only when the old marker is set)
```

and resolves prompt names over `LEGION_PROMPT_ROOTS` (colon-separated, both roots in a pod; unset in a pane) as `explicit: roots`.

`bootgate.go`:
- `pluginPackage = "@sjawhar/pi-legion"`, new `envoyPackage = "@sjawhar/pi-envoy"`, `legacyPackage = "@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy"`; `pluginManifestPath` ends in `@sjawhar/pi-legion/package.json`; every refusal string says `pi-legion` where it said `pi-legion-envoy`; the success log reads `boot gate: pi-legion speaks this daemon's contract and loads with pi-envoy` with fields `lane`, `manifest`, `version`, `daemonApiVersion`, `envoyInterface`, `envoyFrom`. (`scripts/e2e/stage2-tmux-supervision.sh:403` greps the pass line; it changes with it.)
- `pluginGate` gains `envoyPluginRoot string` (pod lane only). `pluginLane` gains `envoyAbsent func(legionVersion string) error`, `envoyMismatch func(found, expected int, from string) error`, `legacyLoaded func(from string) error`, each with its own words per lane:
  - pod: "pi-legion %s loaded from %s, but no pi-envoy loaded from %s, the second explicit extension a pod passes: the worker image is incomplete; build it from this daemon's commit" / "… pi-envoy at %s publishes plugin interface %d; the pi-legion at %s speaks %d: build the worker image from this daemon's commit" / "the worker image loads @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy from %s beside pi-legion: build the worker image from this daemon's commit".
  - pane: "pi-legion %s is loaded in a pane of %s, but no pi-envoy is: install the @sjawhar/pi-envoy release built from this daemon's commit into %s" / "… pi-envoy at %s publishes plugin interface %d; pi-legion speaks %d: install both releases built from this daemon's commit into %s" / "a pane of %s still loads @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy from %s: run `%s plugin uninstall @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy`" (the profile-prefixed `omp` as `notLoaded` already builds it).
  - controller (today's lane has only `flags` and `notLoaded`): "Oh My Pi, launched as the controller launches it (%q, in %s), loaded pi-legion but no pi-envoy.
